html:
The nomad cultures of the steppe north of the Black Sea in the early Iron Age, just before and as the Scythians took over. The map shows them in 700 BCE.

Archaeologists find here, from about 900 to 650 BCE, rich horsemen's graves with bronze bits, cheek-pieces, arrowheads and weapons. Greek writers called the people of this time the Cimmerians. Herodotus says the Scythians, arriving from the east, drove the Cimmerians out, and that the Cimmerians fled into Anatolia, where Assyrian records do place them in the 7th century BCE.

By about 650 BCE the classic Scythian style had arrived, with animal art and huge kurgans; similar early burials in the Altai and Tuva suggest the Scythian way of life began further east. To the north, the farming Chernoles culture held the forest steppe. What followed is told under Scythians and Saka.
